blog.title: 2020 in Review: Still Thankful
blog.description: A month-by-month look back at my 2020: the friends, family, and small moments that made a pandemic year worth being thankful for.

blog.title: 5 things I love about my website (and how they're built)
blog.description: I walk through five things I love about my website, including automatic dark mode, Next.js server rendering, whimsy, and GitHub as my backend.

blog.title: AI Evals: How to Build an LLM Judge That Agrees With You
blog.description: AI evals are fuzzy unit tests. My AI Engineer World's Fair workshop, written up: build an LLM judge, catch its biases and gate deploys on it.

blog.title: Aleph Alpha Kolibri: How the Sovereign German LLM Works
blog.description: Kolibri is Aleph Alpha's open-weight German and English LLM: 78B parameters, 3.5B per token. How it works, what it's good and bad at, and when to use it.

blog.title: The Apple Watch Readiness Score Is Wrong so I Built My Own
blog.description: My Apple Watch told me to Go For It on my most run-down mornings. Why the Readiness score misses and the readiness app I built in 5 days.

blog.title: Biggest Lessons of 2024: Honor, Trauma, and People
blog.description: Dissecting honor, what it takes to overcome trauma, how to heal from the fear of failure and prioritize relationships.

blog.title: Can AI Feel Pain? Why Anthropic Banned Cruelty to Claude
blog.description: Nobody can prove AI feels pain, but 25 open models have a pain direction that rises when you insult them. What it shows and why they're still machines.

blog.title: It's Okay to Code on Nights and Weekends
blog.description: I love coding on nights and weekends because it's my favorite hobby. It only becomes a problem when it turns into a god or an expectation.

blog.title: Bar Raiser Interviews, OKRs, the Spotify Model and Agile: Companies Are Full of It
blog.description: My case against bar raiser interviews, Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), the Spotify model and agile, why AI makes it urgent and how I'd hire instead.

blog.title: Goodbye Facebook
blog.description: Why I'm deleting Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp: FOMO, lost time, and engagement algorithms that radicalize people. I'm moving to Signal instead.

blog.title: Health, Fitness, DevRel, and Hemophilia
blog.description: A deeply personal post about my health journey and how it's affected my fitness, devrel work, and more.

blog.title: Hello World
blog.description: My first post here: a quick hello world I published to make sure the blog works. The real writing starts after this one.

blog.title: How Long Should a Keynote Speaker Speak?
blog.description: A keynote runs 20 to 45 minutes, most often 30. What the attention research really says, what conferences schedule, and how to use the slot you get.

blog.title: How Much Does a Keynote Speaker Cost?
blog.description: A keynote speaker costs $2,500 at the median in 2026 and $10,000 to $25,000 for an established author, plus travel. The benchmarks and what moves them.

blog.title: How to Grow Professional Relationships
blog.description: My TJS model maps professional relationships across seven states, from zero-sum competition to toxic enmeshment, and why collaboration is the peak.

blog.title: Pillars of Impact for Web Engineers
blog.description: I break down the four pillars of impact for web engineers: emotional, social, creative, and technical, and how to grow each one over time.

blog.title: Kolibri vs Claude Sonnet 5.5: A German LLM Benchmark
blog.description: Aleph Alpha's Kolibri lost all 136 blind comparisons to Claude Sonnet 5.5 at German Bible deep dives, despite clean grammar and a leaner tokenizer.

blog.title: Local LLM vs Cloud: Is an $18,000 AI Server Worth It?
blog.description: I've run models on my phone, my laptop and rented GPUs. An $18,000 AI server wins on privacy and loses on price unless it's busy all day.

blog.title: Frontier Models Suck Sometimes (A Benchmark)
blog.description: Apple Intelligence refused my voice note, so I benchmarked 11 AI models on it. A cheap one beat the frontier and my phone's Qwen made things up.

blog.title: Please Stop the Slop: What AI Slop Is and How to Spot It
blog.description: My verdict on AI slop: what it is, how to spot it, why not all AI is slop and a petition to keep the internet human.

blog.title: AI Is Now SI: Super Intelligence Isn't Superior
blog.description: US agencies now call AI Super Intelligence (SI), yet its definition didn't change. What it beats people at, where it fails, and why people make idols.

blog.title: What Are Open Weights? Why People Want GPT-4o Released
blog.description: Open weights means you can download a model and run it yourself. What the GPT-4o petition is really asking, and why releasing the weights is the hard part.

blog.title: What Does the Bible Say About AI?
blog.description: The Bible never mentions AI, but it says plenty about who we are, what we make and who we trust. An AI engineer who builds a Bible app on what that means.

blog.title: What I Learned From Getting Pushed Off My Bicycle
blog.description: A blog post about things I learned after being randomly attacked on the streets of Berlin when a stranger pushed me off my bicycle.

blog.title: What Is an Agent Harness? Harness Engineering Explained
blog.description: An agent harness is everything around an AI model that grounds it in reality: tools, context, guardrails, the loop and verification. How to build one.

blog.title: What Is Good Taste in Software? How to Develop It
blog.description: Good taste in software is a trainable skill: judging quality against external standards. 6 practice protocols, with the research under each one.

blog.title: What Is React Fiber? How React Works Under the Hood
blog.description: React Fiber is how React has rendered since version 16: a tree of small units of work it can pause and resume. How it works, from the React source.

blog.title: What Is WebMCP? How My Website Gives AI Agents Tools
blog.description: WebMCP is a proposed web standard that lets a page give AI agents tools to call. How tej.as offers agents 4 of them, and what WebMCP is good for.

blog.title: Why AI Can't Replace Human Taste and Creativity
blog.description: AI can't replace human creativity or taste: we crave novelty and a model makes what's most common. My answer to a question after my talk in Prague.

blog.title: Why I Don't Prefer Speaking at Remote Conferences
blog.description: Why I'd rather not speak at virtual conferences during COVID-19: the hallway conversations are the point, and video calls lose that connection.

blog.title: Why I Think Remote Work is Incredible
blog.description: Two months into my first fully remote job, I compare it with office life: deeper focus, better health, and the sleep rhythm trap I had to fix.
